# ___Input_data___

```{r}
fetahu2023 <- readRDS(file = paste0(params$out,"Rds/fetahu2023_withMetadata.Rds"))
ALL_NK <- readRDS(file = paste0(params$out,"Rds/fetahu2023_NK_cluster.Rds"))
crinier2021 <- readRDS(file = paste0(params$input_BM1))
```

```{r}
Idents(ALL_NK) <- ALL_NK@meta.data$sample
ALL_NK <- RenameIdents(ALL_NK, 
                    "2005_1702" = "ATRXmut_01", 
                    "2006_2684" = "sporadic_01",
                    "2014_0102" = "ctrl_01",
                    "2016_1853" = "ctrl_02",
                    "2016_2950" = "ctrl_03",
                    "2016_3924" = "ATRXmut_02",
                    "2016_4503" = "MYCNA_01",
                    "2018_1404" = "MYCNA_02",
                    "2018_1625" = "sporadic_02",
                    "2018_4252" = "ctrl_04",
                    "2018_6056" = "sporadic_03",
                    "2019_2495" = "sporadic_04",
                    "2019_5022" = "MYCNA_03",
                    "2019_5754" = "MYCNA_04",
                    "2020_1288" = "ctrl_05",
                    "2020_1667" = "sporadic_05")

ALL_NK@meta.data$patients <- Idents(ALL_NK)

ALL_NK <- 
  ALL_NK %>% 
  NormalizeData(normalization.method = "LogNormalize",
                scale.factor = 10000)

crinier2021 <- 
  crinier2021 %>% 
  NormalizeData(normalization.method = "LogNormalize",
                scale.factor = 10000)


# Crinier et al., 2021 as reference
NK_clusters <- crinier2021$cluster2
original_clusters <- ALL_NK$orig.ident

fetahu2023_NK_mat <- GetAssayData(ALL_NK, 
                        assay = "RNA", 
                        slot = "data")

crinier2021_mat <- GetAssayData(crinier2021, 
                            assay = "RNA", 
                            slot = "data")
```

```{r}
# Store de.n values [Number of DE genes] from 5 to 500 with a 10 step incrament
de_n_values <- seq(5, 500, by=10) 

# store results
results <- data.frame(de_n = integer(), cluster = character(), num_cells = integer())

# Loop through de.n values
for (de_n in de_n_values) {
 
  # Run SingleR with the current de.n parameter
  singleR_result <- SingleR(test = fetahu2023_NK_mat, 
                            ref = crinier2021_mat, 
                            labels = NK_clusters, 
                            de.n = de_n,
                            num.threads = 80)
  
  # Get the number of cells per cluster
  cluster_counts <- table(singleR_result$labels)
  
  # Add the results to the data frame
  results <- rbind(results, data.frame(de_n = de_n, 
                                       cluster = names(cluster_counts), 
                                       num_cells = as.integer(cluster_counts)))
}

# Plot the results using ggplot2
ggplot(results, aes(x = de_n, y = num_cells, color = cluster)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  labs(title = "Number of cells per cluster vs. de.n parameter",
       x = "de.n parameter",
       y = "Number of cells per cluster") +
  theme_minimal()
```


```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(reshape2)

#  range for de.n parameter
de_n_values <- seq(5, 500, by=10)  

# Initialize a list to store results
results_list <- list()

# Loop through de.n values
for (de_n in de_n_values) {
  
  # Run SingleR with the current de.n parameter
  singleR_result <- SingleR(test = fetahu2023_NK_mat, 
                            ref = crinier2021_mat, 
                            labels = NK_clusters, 
                            de.n = de_n,
                            num.threads = 80)
  
  # Store the results in a list, using de.n as the name
  results_list[[as.character(de_n)]] <- singleR_result$labels
}

# Convert the results list to a data frame
results_df <- do.call(cbind, results_list)
colnames(results_df) <- de_n_values
results_df <- as.data.frame(results_df)
results_df$de_n <- colnames(results_df)
results_df$Cell_ID <- rownames(results_df)

# Melt the data frame for plotting
results_melted <- melt(results_df, 
                       id.vars = "Cell_ID", 
                       variable.name = "de_n", 
                       value.name = "Predicted_Type")

results_melted

# Make sure de.n is treated as a numeric variable
results_melted$de_n <- as.numeric(as.character(results_melted$de_n))

# Plot the heatmap
ggplot(results_melted, aes(x = de_n, y = Cell_ID, fill = Predicted_Type)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = COLOR_CODE_v2) +
  labs(title = "Heatmap of predicted NK sub-types across different de.n values",
       x = "de.n parameter",
       y = "Cell ID",
       fill = "Predicted NK Type") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(),  # Optional: Hide y-axis text if there are too many cells
        axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid = element_blank())
```

```{r subsampled}
set.seed(123)
num_cells <- nrow(results_df)

# If the number of cells is greater than 500, sub-sample
if (num_cells > 500) {
  # Randomly sample 500 cell IDs
  sampled_cell_ids <- sample(results_df$Cell_ID, 500, replace = FALSE)
  
  # Subset results_df to include only the sampled cells
  results_df_subsampled <- results_df[results_df$Cell_ID %in% sampled_cell_ids, ]
} else {
  # If there are fewer than 500 cells, use the entire dataset
  results_df_subsampled <- results_df
  warning("The number of cells is less than or equal to 500; using the entire dataset.")
}

# Display the first few rows of the subsampled data frame
head(results_df_subsampled)

# Melt the data frame for plotting
df_subsampled_melted <- melt(results_df_subsampled, 
                       id.vars = "Cell_ID", 
                       variable.name = "de_n", 
                       value.name = "Predicted_Type")

df_subsampled_melted

# Make sure de.n is treated as a numeric variable
df_subsampled_melted$de_n <- as.numeric(as.character(df_subsampled_melted$de_n))

# Plot the heatmap
ggplot(df_subsampled_melted, aes(x = de_n, y = Cell_ID, fill = Predicted_Type)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = COLOR_CODE_v2) +
  labs(title = "Heatmap of predicted NK sub-types across different de.n values",
       x = "de.n parameter",
       y = "Cell ID",
       fill = "Predicted NK Type") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(),  # Optional: Hide y-axis text if there are too many cells
        axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid = element_blank())

```
